prompt.text: Which phylum is the only animal phylum that is not eumetazoan?

questions.explanation: Eumetazoans are animals with true tissues. Porifera, the sponges, is the only animal phylum outside that group. A sponge has no true tissues and no true germ layers. Cnidaria have true tissues. A cnidarian forms two germ layers, the ectoderm and the endoderm. Platyhelminthes, the flatworms, have three germ layers. Arthropoda have three germ layers, and an arthropod sheds a tough external cuticle as it grows. Those three phyla are eumetazoans.

prompt.text: Select every trait that unifies the eumetazoans.

bank: Embryos with distinct germ layers
A fluid-filled body cavity lined on all sides by mesoderm
True tissues
A cuticle that is shed as the animal grows
True body symmetry
A backbone of vertebrae
answers: Embryos with distinct germ layers
True tissues
True body symmetry
questions.explanation: Three traits unify the eumetazoans. Their embryos form distinct germ layers. They have true tissues. Their bodies have true symmetry, either parts arranged around a central axis or a left side that mirrors the right. Porifera, the sponges, lack all three, which is why that phylum is not eumetazoan. A fluid-filled cavity lined on all sides by mesoderm is a coelom. A cnidarian and a flatworm are eumetazoans, and neither has that cavity. A cuticle that is shed as the animal grows unites the ecdysozoans, such as a nematode and an arthropod. It is not a trait of every eumetazoan. A backbone of vertebrae is a vertebrate trait. A cnidarian is a eumetazoan and has no vertebrae. Distinct germ layers do not mean three layers in every embryo. A cnidarian has two, the ectoderm and the endoderm.

prompt.text: How do sponges reproduce?

options: Most sponges are hermaphrodites and reproduce sexually. They also reproduce asexually by budding or fragmentation.
Sponges reproduce only sexually. Each sponge is either male or female, and it never makes both eggs and sperm.
Sponges reproduce only asexually, by budding. They do not make eggs or sperm.
Sponges release spores, and a spore grows into a new sponge without fertilization.
questions.answer: Most sponges are hermaphrodites and reproduce sexually. They also reproduce asexually by budding or fragmentation.
questions.explanation: Most sponges are hermaphrodites. One sponge makes both eggs and sperm, often acting as one sex and then the other. Most sponges have hermaphroditic gonads, which produce both eggs and sperm. Eggs develop from amoebocytes, and sperm develop from choanocytes. Sperm are released into the water and drawn into another sponge, where fertilization occurs. The zygote develops into a flagellated larva. That larva is sexually immature, its body differs from the sessile adult, and it settles and becomes the adult. Sponges also reproduce asexually. A bud or a fragment can grow into a new sponge. Freshwater sponges can form gemmules, clusters of cells that survive harsh conditions and later grow. A sponge is not locked into one sex. Asexual budding does not replace eggs and sperm. A sponge does not release spores.

questions.explanation: Sponges have spicules, amoebocytes, choanocytes, spongin, and hermaphroditic gonads. A choanocyte is a flagellated collar cell that draws water through the sponge and traps food. An amoebocyte is a mobile cell that digests food, carries nutrients, and produces skeletal material. Spicules are hard skeletal elements of calcium carbonate or silica. Spongin is a network of flexible protein fibers. A sponge may be supported by spicules, by spongin, or by both. Most sponges have hermaphroditic gonads, which produce both eggs and sperm. A nematocyst is a stinging capsule of a cnidarian. A gastrovascular cavity is the digestive sac of a cnidarian. A sponge has neither one.

prompt.text: In a sponge, what does a choanocyte do?

options: Its flagellum draws water through the sponge, and its collar traps food.
It moves through the body, digests food, carries nutrients, and produces skeletal material.
It is a hard skeletal element made of calcium carbonate or silica.
It is a network of flexible protein fibers that supports the body.
It produces both eggs and sperm.
questions.answer: Its flagellum draws water through the sponge, and its collar traps food.
questions.explanation: A choanocyte is a collar cell. A flagellum surrounded by a collar of microvilli beats and draws water through small pores and out through a larger opening, the osculum. The collar traps food particles from that current. An amoebocyte then digests the food, carries nutrients, and can produce the skeleton. A spicule is a hard skeletal element of calcium carbonate or silica. Spongin is a network of flexible protein fibers. A hermaphroditic gonad produces both eggs and sperm. Sperm develop from choanocytes, but the choanocyte's job in feeding is the current and the collar. A choanocyte is not the skeleton.

prompt.text: In a sponge, what does an amoebocyte do?

options: It moves through the body, digests food, carries nutrients, and produces skeletal material.
Its flagellum draws water through the sponge, and its collar traps food.
It is a hard skeletal element made of calcium carbonate or silica.
It is a network of flexible protein fibers that supports the body.
It produces both eggs and sperm.
questions.answer: It moves through the body, digests food, carries nutrients, and produces skeletal material.
questions.explanation: An amoebocyte moves through the mesohyl, the gelatinous layer inside the sponge. It takes food from choanocytes, digests it, and carries nutrients to other cells. It also produces spicules and spongin, and it can become other kinds of cells. Another name for this cell is an archaeocyte. Eggs develop from amoebocytes inside the hermaphroditic gonads. A choanocyte uses its flagellum and collar to draw water through the sponge and trap food. A spicule is a hard skeletal element of calcium carbonate or silica. Spongin is a network of flexible protein fibers. A hermaphroditic gonad produces both eggs and sperm. The amoebocyte makes skeletal material and can give rise to eggs. It is not itself the skeleton or the gonad.

options: It is a hard skeletal element made of calcium carbonate or silica.
Its flagellum draws water through the sponge, and its collar traps food.
It moves through the body, digests food, carries nutrients, and produces skeletal material.

questions.answer: It is a hard skeletal element made of calcium carbonate or silica.
questions.explanation: A spicule supports the sponge. It is a hard element made of calcium carbonate or silica, and it can also make the sponge difficult to eat. Amoebocytes produce spicules. Spongin is the other kind of support, a network of flexible protein fibers. A sponge may have spicules, spongin, or both. A choanocyte draws water through the sponge and traps food. An amoebocyte digests that food and carries nutrients. A hermaphroditic gonad produces both eggs and sperm. None of those is a spicule.

A choanocyte draws water through the sponge and traps food. An amoebocyte digests that food, carries nutrients, and produces the skeleton. A hermaphroditic gonad produces both eggs and sperm. prompt.text: How does a sponge feed?

options: Water enters through pores and passes through canals and chambers lined by choanocytes. The choanocytes trap food, and the water leaves through the osculum.
Water enters through the osculum and passes through canals and chambers. The choanocytes trap food, and the water leaves through the pores.
Food enters a gastrovascular cavity through one opening. Cells lining that cavity digest the food, and waste leaves through the same opening.
Amoebocytes on the outer surface engulf food. Water does not pass through canals or chambers, and the sponge has no osculum.
questions.answer: Water enters through pores and passes through canals and chambers lined by choanocytes. The choanocytes trap food, and the water leaves through the osculum.
questions.explanation: A sponge feeds by filtering water. Water enters through pores, called ostia, and passes through canals and chambers lined by choanocytes. The flagellum of a choanocyte keeps the current moving, and the collar traps food particles. An amoebocyte then digests that food and carries the nutrients. The filtered water leaves through the osculum, a larger opening. The current does not enter through the osculum and leave through the pores. A sponge has no gastrovascular cavity. Amoebocytes digest food inside the body. They do not replace the water path through the canals, the chambers, and the osculum.

prompt.text: What makes Ctenophora unique?

options: Eight rows of comb-like cilia move the animal, and sticky colloblasts capture prey.
A contracting bell moves the animal, and stinging nematocysts capture prey.
Choanocytes draw water through canals and chambers, and the water leaves through an osculum.
A tough external cuticle is shed as the animal grows, and jointed appendages move the body.
questions.answer: Eight rows of comb-like cilia move the animal, and sticky colloblasts capture prey.
questions.explanation: Ctenophora are the comb jellies. Eight rows of fused cilia, called combs, beat and move the animal. That is the trait the phylum is named for. Sticky colloblasts capture prey by releasing adhesive threads. A ctenophore does not make nematocysts. A cnidarian often swims by contracting a bell and captures prey with stinging nematocysts. Its gut is a gastrovascular cavity with one opening. Many ctenophores have a mouth and anal pores, so the gut has two openings. A sponge feeds with choanocytes. Water passes through canals and chambers and leaves through an osculum. An arthropod sheds a tough external cuticle and moves with jointed appendages. Ctenophores have two germ layers, the ectoderm and the endoderm, as a cnidarian does. The combs and the colloblasts are what set Ctenophora apart.

prompt.text: What makes Cnidaria unique?

options: Stinging cells called cnidocytes contain nematocysts, which discharge to capture prey and for defense.
Eight rows of comb-like cilia move the animal, and sticky colloblasts capture prey.
Choanocytes draw water through canals and chambers, and the water leaves through an osculum.
A tough external cuticle is shed as the animal grows, and jointed appendages move the body.
questions.answer: Stinging cells called cnidocytes contain nematocysts, which discharge to capture prey and for defense.
questions.explanation: Cnidaria are the jellies, sea anemones, corals, and hydrozoans. Stinging cells called cnidocytes are unique to this phylum, and the phylum is named for them. A capsule inside each cnidocyte, the nematocyst, discharges to capture prey and for defense. The body is a sac with a gastrovascular cavity. One opening serves as both mouth and anus. A cnidarian has two germ layers, the ectoderm and the endoderm. The two body forms are the polyp, which is sessile, and the medusa, which swims. A sea anemone and a coral live as polyps. A jellyfish is a medusa. Some hydrozoans have both forms, and some cnidarians have only one. Eight rows of comb-like cilia and sticky colloblasts belong to Ctenophora, the comb jellies. A ctenophore does not make nematocysts. Choanocytes, canals, chambers, and an osculum are how a sponge feeds. An arthropod sheds a tough external cuticle and moves with jointed appendages.

A nematocyst inside each cnidocyte discharges to capture prey and for defense. Triploblastic means three germ layers, including a mesoderm. Bilateral symmetry means a left side that mirrors the right. A cnidarian has neither of those traits, and it has no organs.

questions.explanation: A polyp is sessile and cylindrical. Its mouth and tentacles point up, and the other end is attached to a surface. A sea anemone and a coral live as polyps. A medusa is free-swimming and bell-shaped. Its mouth and tentacles point down, and it moves by contracting the bell. A jellyfish is a medusa. The two descriptions are not reversed. Some hydrozoans have both forms, and some cnidarians have only one.

prompt.text: True or false: A sessile cnidarian polyp can move.

questions.explanation: A sessile cnidarian polyp can move. Sessile means it lives attached to a surface. It does not mean the body is frozen. The polyp can bend, contract, and move its tentacles. A sea anemone can also creep slowly along that surface. A hydra can somersault and attach in a new place. A coral polyp stays fixed to the colony, but it can still extend and retract. This movement is not the free swimming of a medusa. A medusa is bell-shaped and swims with its mouth and tentacles pointing down.

prompt.text: A hydrozoan spends part of its life attached as a polyp and part of its life as a free-swimming medusa. What is the benefit of each form?

options: The polyp stays in a feeding spot and the colony grows by budding. The medusa reproduces sexually and disperses to new places.
The polyp swims away and reproduces sexually. The medusa stays attached, feeds, and the colony grows by budding.
Both forms stay attached and feed. Neither form reproduces or disperses.
Both forms swim and reproduce sexually. Neither form stays in place to feed and grow.
questions.answer: The polyp stays in a feeding spot and the colony grows by budding. The medusa reproduces sexually and disperses to new places.
questions.explanation: In a hydrozoan with both stages, the polyp and the medusa do different jobs. The polyp remains attached in a place where it can feed. It can still bend, creep, or move its tentacles, but it does not leave to disperse. New polyps bud from the colony, so the colony grows without sex. The medusa is the free-swimming form. It produces eggs and sperm, and it can carry that sexual reproduction to a new place. A larva, the planula, settles and grows into a polyp. The two jobs are not reversed. A sea anemone and a coral have the polyp form only. A jellyfish may live as a medusa. This split of feeding and growth from sexual dispersal applies to a hydrozoan that has both forms.

options: Some members have a lophophore, a crown of ciliated tentacles used for feeding, and some have a trochophore larva.

questions.answer: Some members have a lophophore, a crown of ciliated tentacles used for feeding, and some have a trochophore larva.

Lophotrochozoans are protostomes, so the mouth develops from the blastopore. They are the other large protostome group beside the ecdysozoans. Shedding a cuticle is the ecdysozoan trait, as in a nematode or an arthropod. Comb rows and colloblasts belong to Ctenophora. Cnidocytes belong to Cnidaria.

prompt.text: What is a visceral mass?

options: The part of a mollusc that contains most of the internal organs.
The muscular part of a mollusc that is used for movement.
A fold of tissue that drapes over the internal organs and secretes the shell.
The fluid-filled body cavity lined on all sides by mesoderm.
questions.answer: The part of a mollusc that contains most of the internal organs.
questions.explanation: A visceral mass is the part of a mollusc that contains most of the internal organs. A snail, a clam, and a squid each have one. The other two parts of the mollusc body are the foot and the mantle. The foot is muscular and is used for movement. The mantle is a fold of tissue that drapes over the visceral mass and secretes the shell, if one is present. The fluid-filled body cavity lined on all sides by mesoderm is the coelom. In a mollusc the coelom is reduced. In most molluscs the circulatory system is open, so the main body cavity is a hemocoel. A squid or an octopus has a closed circulatory system, and the blood stays in vessels. Neither cavity is the visceral mass.
